The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 03.05.2023.
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That on 07.02.2023 at about 8.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-KH-3115 on Mandanapalli - Tirupathi Road and when he reached near H.P. Petrol Bunk, Madanapali Mandal, Annamayya SCCH-10 Dist,
Andhra Pradesh, at that time, the driver of the Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.
No.AP-03-TE-4736 came from opposite direction with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's Motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the injured petitioner was shifted to hospital and took inpatient treatment.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident, he could not do his work, he became permanently disabled and put to irreparable loss of income.
The respondent No.1 being owner and the respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
the present petition.
3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 though appeared before the Court, have not filed the written statement.

My predecessor in office after recording the evidence of the petitioner has passed the judgment dated 04.03.2024 by holding that the petitioner is entitled for SCCH-10 compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. and directed the respondent No.2 insurance company to deposit the compensation amount.

The respondent No.2 has filed petition in Misc.
No.555/2024 and the Tribunal as per order dated 05.08.2024 pleased to restore the MVC No.1558/2023 to its original file.
Chandu.

4. After restoration of the claim petition, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the Court and filed the written statement.
Despite giving sufficient opportunity the respondent No.1 has not filed written statement.

. 
5. The brief contentions of the respondent No.2 (insurer) are as under:
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TE- 4736 in the name of respondent No.1 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident,
however the liability if any subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, since the petitioner was minor and was not SCCH-10 possessing driving licence the accident caused due to his negligent act.

Further,
denied the accident, the manner in which the accident took place, rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and its involvement in the alleged accident.

Further, the respondent No.2 has denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident, treatment taken for those injuries, medical expenses incurred and permanent disability suffered by him and also denied the age,
avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent No.2 prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Passenger Autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TE- 4736 by its driver

, in RTA took place on 07.02.2023 at about 8.00 p.m., near HP petrol SCCH-10 bunk, on Madanapalli - Thirupathi Main Road, Madanapalli Mandal, Kasiraopeta Village,
Annamayya, Andhra Pradesh ?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what amount and from whom ?
3) What order or award?
7.

Initially, father of the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and during the pendency of the petition, since the petitioner attained the age of majority, he was examined himself as PW-2 and also examined the doctor as PW-3 and in all got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.

The respondent No.2 has examined the doctor as RW-1 and also its official as RW-2 and in all got marked documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.
8.
Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

My findings to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative SCCH-10 Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following :
R E A S O N S 10. ISSUE No.1:
The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 07.02.2023.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR No.43/2023 of Madanapalle Rural PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement along with its Kannada translation copy.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that I.O. has registered a case against the driver of the Passenger Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TE-4736 for the commission of offences punishable under Sec. 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of charge sheet filed by the Madanapalle Rural PS.

On perusal of Ex.P.5, it reveals that, after investigation the police have filed charge sheet against one Mr. Patan Sayed Khan, who is none other than the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 338 of IPC.
SCCH-10 11.
Further, as per wound certificate i.e. Ex.P.4 produced by petitioner and Ex.P.6 discharge summary, it appears that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.

12. As discussed supra, the IO after investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle showing him as an accused in the said case and as per the police records, it reveal that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and has caused the accident.
Further, there is no document to show that the petitioner was negligent in riding his bike and accident occurred due to his negligent act.
13. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of SCCH-10 negligence is not required

. This view is supported by the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

sentences.text: Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that, the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash driving of the driver of the Passenger Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TE-4736.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2:-

The petitioner contended that, after the accident, he was shifted to Government hospital, Voyalpadu and after first aid and for further treatment he was shifted to Ramadevi Multi Speciality hospital, Thirupati, wherein he took inpatient treatment.
SCCH-10 16.

Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar.
In para No.5 of the judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has mentioned the heads under which compensation is to be awarded in personal injury cases.
I reproduce the same hereunder for convenience.

Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising):
 Loss of earning during the period of
treatment

; 
b. Loss of future earning on account of permanent disability.
Future Medical expenses.
SCCH-10 Non-pecuniary damages (general damages) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
Loss of amenities (and / or loss of prospects of marriage) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
Keeping in view the law declared in the aforementioned decision, I have carefully perused the entire materials placed on record.
The wound certificate of the petitioner has been marked as Ex.P.5.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Chandu.

sentences.text: In this case, the petitioner has produced discharge card as per Ex.P.6.

On perusal of Ex.P.6 it reveals that, the petitioner was admitted to the Ramadevi Multi Speciality hospital, Thirupati on 08.02.2023 and discharged on 20.02.2023 and it also discloses that, the petitioner has sustained head injury and other injuries all over the body.
18. Ex.P.10 are the medical bills amounting to Rs.2,66,073/- and Ex.P.7 are the medical prescriptions.
The SCCH-10 medical bills produced by the petitioner appears to be genuine.

Hence,
the petitioner is entitled for actual medical bills and same is rounded off to Rs.2,66,000/- under the head of Medical expenses.
19. As per the medical documents it appear that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he is suffering from physical disability.
By considering the nature of injury, the petitioner might have suffered pain and agony.
Considering the age of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that if Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards pain and sufferings it would be just.
If Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards nourishment and diet food it would be just.
20. The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury he under went conservative line of treatment and he is suffering from permanent disability and neurological deficit.
He has further stated that, due to the disability he has lost his earning capacity.

In order to establish the disability,
the doctor was examined before the Court as PW-3.

PW-3 during SCCH-10 his evidence has deposed that, recently for assessment of disability, he examined the petitioner on 08.03.2025 and on examination it is found that, the petitioner is a conscious ambulant patient with impaired memory,
CT brain revealed gliotic changes in left cerebellum and right frontal region.
Further, the petitioner has neuro disability pertaining to cognition and the disability is around 20% and the disability pertains to his whole body and is likely to be permanent.
Though PW-3 doctor was cross-examined by the counsel for the respondent No.3, nothing was elicited from the mouth of the witness to disprove his evidence.
21. According to the petitioner, he was aged about 17 years at the time of accident.
There is no proof of avocation and income of the petitioner.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration.

At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4)
KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

sentences.text: In the above decision the SCCH-10 Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.

As per the said notional income chart, the income for the year 2022 is fixed as Rs.15,500/- Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the petitioner would be just and proper.
The accident was occurred on 07.02.2023.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,000/- as monthly income of the petitioner.
22. On perusal of the medical documents and medical evidence it is crystal clear that, the petitioner cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.

Hence, the disability of the petitioner would Chandu.S vs Sonakanti Mokshgna Sai Venkat on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147347516/

sentences.text: 23. According to the doctor, the petitioner is suffering from 20% neuro disability and it pertains to the whole body.
It is settled principles that all permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.

Even though the doctor has opined 20% permanent disability to the whole body, considering the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity as 15%.
24. To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.9.
As per Ex.P.9, the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 05.04.2006.
The accident was occurred on 07.02.2023.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is considered as 17 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable for his age is 18.
The loss of future earning SCCH-10 capacity is assessed as 15%.
The annual income is assessed Rs.1,92,000/-(Rs.16,000 x 12).
Therefore, the loss of future income would be Rs.1,92,000/-(annual income) X 18 (multiplier) X 15% = Rs.5,18,400/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income of Rs.5,18,400/-.
25.
The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury and disability he is unable to do any physical strain works and the disability is coming in the way of his day today activities and avocation.

Hence,
considering the injuries suffered, this Court is of the opinion that, due to disability, the petitioner must forego some comforts in his life.
Hence, I conclude that if Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities it would be just.

26. Thus, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads;
Sl.
 Heads Compensation No.
1) Medical expenses Rs. 2,66,000 /-
2) Pain and sufferings Rs. 30,000/-
 SCCH-10 3) Nourishment and diet food Rs. 15,000 /-
 Loss of Future earning Rs. 5,18,400/-
4) capacity due to permanent  disability 5) Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000 /-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.8,59,400/-.
27. REGARDING LIABILITY:

As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Passenger Chandu.S vs Sonakanti Mokshgna Sai Venkat on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147347516/

In this case, the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.2, as such, respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of the accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 RC owner of the vehicle and respondent No.2 insurer are jointly and severally SCCH-10 liable to satisfy the award.

28. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 while canvassing the arguments has submitted that, the petitioner being minor was riding the motor cycle in a public road without possessing valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.

As per Section 3 of Motor Vehicles Act,
no person shall drive Motor Vehicle in any public place unless he holds an effective driving licence issued by the competent authority.
As per Section 4 of the Motor Vehicles Act, no person under the age of 18 years shall drive a motor cycle in a public place.
29. As per the records it reveal that, the petitioner who is minor riding the Bullet Motor cycle without possessing valid and effective diving licence as on the date of accident.
Therefore, he was also negligent and contributed for the cause of alleged accident.
Considering the circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, his negligence is taken to an extent of 10%.

Therefore,
this Tribunal has assessed the contributory negligence in the ratio of 90:10 i.e. SCCH-10 90%
negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TE-4736 and 10% negligence contributed by the petitioner.
Hence, out of the total compensation, the petitioner is entitled for 90% of the compensation awarded i.e. a sum of Rs.7,73,460/-.

The respondent No.2 being insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation of Rs.7,73,460/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.

Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
30.
Issue No.3:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,73,460/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
SCCH-10
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.2 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Out of the award amount, 25% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 2 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through NEFT / RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-

Issue No.3:
In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,73,460/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
SCCH-10
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.2 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Out of the award amount, 25% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 2 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through NEFT / RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.
